category_title: Students with severe disabilities who use shouting and aggression to communicate basic needs
student_description: This student has severe communication barriers and relies on aggression, crying, or inappropriate laughter when their primary needs are misunderstood or when faced with abrupt environmental changes. They uniquely require alternative communication systems (like PECS or signs) and multimodal support, as traditional verbal-only methods fail and trigger severe frustration.

criteria.rationale: Building communication skills gradually equips the student to become an independent initiator of communication without becoming overwhelmed.
criteria.check: The tutor's long-term plan outlines a step-by-step progression from basic, simple communication exchanges to more complex, functional interactions.

criteria.rationale: A sustained focus on nonverbal communication ensures the student has accessible tools to express themselves, avoiding the failure of verbal-only speech therapy.
criteria.check: The tutor's long-term strategy explicitly incorporates the simultaneous development of nonverbal communication systems (e.g., PECS, signs) alongside any other educational goals.
